proposals.evidence: Perder example 7 glosses yat remembrance in names are remembered. Platts Persian yād has remembrance and yād honā be remembered. Final t can be compared with Perder’s discussion of final devoicing (pp. 43–44), but the unmarked vowel length and immediate donor remain unresolved. The Pashto plural on adjacent nam-una is contact context, not proof that yat itself was borrowed directly from Pashto.
